intro: FBX to OBJ converts 3D models from FBX to OBJ on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to open an FBX in a program or viewer that does not support it. OBJ is the exchange format opened by Blender, viewers and almost every 3D program, with several parts and, with its MTL, colours.

FBX is Autodesk's format used by Maya, 3ds Max, Blender, Unity and Unreal to exchange models and scenes. As FBX uses the Y axis up and 3D printing uses Z, the model is turned so it stands upright in the slicer; if you do not want that, tick “Keep the original axes” in the advanced options. FBX is read by assimp in an isolated process with no access to the rest of the server: textures and animations are not converted, only the geometry and each material's colour.

You can apply a scale, choose the original's units if the FBX does not store them and decide what to do with the parts: keep them separate inside the OBJ when the format allows it, merge them into one mesh or get one file per part in a ZIP.

The FBX geometry reaches the OBJ without being simplified or repaired. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, and up to ten files per task; they are processed on our server in the European Union and deleted when they expire.
steps: Upload one or more FBX files.
Choose the units and, optionally, the scale and parts.

faq.q: Why does the OBJ come out rotated or on its side?
faq.a: Because FBX and OBJ may use different axes. Try ticking or unticking “Keep the original axes” in the advanced options.
The FBX material colours go into the OBJ if the format supports them; STL stores no colours and the note says so.

faq.q: What if the model has holes?
faq.a: The OBJ has the same geometry as the FBX. To close them before printing, use Repair STL.
